title: Same body numerically: seven proofs against Origenists
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): The subject-quod stand as all who stand as to rise. Against ye Origenist delirium Gregory ye Great disputed. 15:50 hinder — flesh plus blood stand as barred under ye name belonging toward guilt, not substance. Nor does 1 Cor. (7) out from ye double rite belonging toward baptism plus burial. (6) out from ye promise belonging toward immortality to this flesh; (5) out from Christ's example plus nine particular examples; (4) because death stands as called sleep plus resurrection awakening; (3) out from ye very name — otherwise a new creation, not resurrection; (2) out from God's justice (Ambrose); 5:10; 2 Cor. 3:21; Phil. 15:53; 1 Cor. 10:28; The body such that will rise stands as ye same in number plus substance: (1) Matt.
pass_b_english: The body that will rise is the same in number and substance: (1) Matt. 10:28; 1 Cor. 15:53; Phil. 3:21; 2 Cor. 5:10; (2) from God's justice (Ambrose); (3) from the very name — otherwise a new creation, not resurrection; (4) because death is called sleep and resurrection awakening; (5) from Christ's example and nine particular examples; (6) from the promise of immortality to this flesh; (7) from the double rite of baptism and burial. Nor does 1 Cor. 15:50 hinder — flesh and blood are barred under the name of guilt, not substance. Against the Origenist delirium Gregory the Great disputed. The subject-quod are all who are to rise.
source_text: Corpus resurrecturum numero & substantia idem: 1. Matth. 10.28; 1 Cor. 15.53; Phil. 3.21; 2 Cor. 5.10. 2. ex justitia Dei (Ambrosius). 3. ab ipsa appellatione — alioquin nova creatio, non resurrectio. 4. quia mors somnus, resurrectio evigilatio. 5. ab exemplo Christi & novem particularibus exemplis. 6. a promissione immortalitatis huic carni. 7. a duplici ritu baptismi & sepulturae. Neque obstat 1 Cor. 15.50 — caro & sanguis nomine culpae arcentur. Contra Origenistarum delirium disputavit Gregorius Magnus. Subjectum quod sunt omnes qui sunt resurrecturi.
